subject: chemistry
title: Solubility product
key_idea: The solubility product, Ksp, is the product of the ion concentrations, each raised to the power of its coefficient, in a saturated solution of a sparingly soluble salt. Adding a common ion lowers the solubility of the salt.

blocks.text: A sparingly soluble salt in water sets up an equilibrium between the solid and its ions. Ksp is the equilibrium constant for this.

items.meaning: The product of the concentrations of the ions of a sparingly soluble salt in a saturated solution, each to the power of its coefficient in the equation.
A solution in which the dissolved ions are in equilibrium with the undissolved solid.

items: The solid is left out, because its concentration is constant.
Each concentration is raised to the power of the number in front of the ion.
Work out the units by putting units into the expression.
Ksp is constant at a given temperature.
Ksp has ion concentrations only, each to the power of its coefficient.
Write the equation first, then the expression and its units.

blocks.text: Link the solubility, s in mol/dm³, to the ion concentrations. Then use the expression in either direction.

items.text: Find each ion concentration from s, then substitute into the Ksp expression.
Put each ion in terms of s, then solve for s.

blocks.text: If the solubility of silver chromate(VI) is 6.5 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³, Ksp = 4 × (6.5 × 10⁻⁵)³ = 1.1 × 10⁻¹² mol³/dm⁹.

diagram.alt: A practice question finding Ksp for silver chromate from its solubility.
diagram.question: The solubility of Ag₂CrO₄ is {x} × 10⁻⁴ mol/dm³. Calculate Ksp in units of 10⁻¹² mol³/dm⁹.

items: Write the ions in terms of s.
Ksp = 4s³ for salts of the type AB₂ or A₂B.

blocks.text: A common ion is an ion that is already in the solution and is also in the salt. This section covers what it does to solubility.

items: Adding a common ion raises its concentration in the solution.
The Ksp expression must stay constant, so the equilibrium shifts towards the solid. Some of the salt precipitates.
The salt is therefore less soluble in a solution containing a common ion than in pure water.
A precipitate forms when the product of the ion concentrations, calculated for the mixture, is greater than Ksp.

blocks.text: In 0.100 mol/dm³ NaCl, [Cl⁻] = 0.100 mol/dm³. For AgCl with Ksp = 1.7 × 10⁻¹⁰, [Ag⁺] = 1.7 × 10⁻¹⁰ ÷ 0.100 = 1.7 × 10⁻⁹ mol/dm³.

items: Ignore the chloride ions that come from AgCl. They are negligible next to the chloride ions from NaCl.
The solubility of AgCl in this solution is equal to [Ag⁺], 1.7 × 10⁻⁹ mol/dm³.
Use the common ion concentration in the Ksp expression to find the other ion.

checks.q: Write the Ksp expression for calcium fluoride, CaF₂, and state its units.
The solubility of lead(II) iodide, PbI₂, is 1.2 × 10⁻³ mol/dm³. Calculate Ksp.
Explain why silver chloride is less soluble in sodium chloride solution than in water.
checks.a: NaCl adds Cl⁻ ions, which are common to AgCl. [Ag⁺][Cl⁻] must stay equal to Ksp, so the equilibrium shifts to the solid and less AgCl dissolves.
